items.title: gos.abilities.command_status
items.text: Read command lifecycle, activation evidence, cleanup and observed outcome.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.abilities.command_status(command_handle)

items.title: Contract and usage
items.text: Ability lookups accept a case-insensitive display name or an exact current opaque ability_handle. Ability metadata is local-player-only.

items.title: gos.abilities.command_status(command_handle)
items.text:
Returns the stable public command state:

{
  known = boolean,
  state = "unknown" | "queued" | "dispatching" | "dispatched" | "native_queued" |
          "accepted" | "targeting" | "synchronizing" | "submitted" |
          "acknowledged" | "failed" | "superseded" | "cancelled" | "abandoned" | "expired",
  terminal = boolean,
  acknowledged = boolean,
  activation_proven = boolean,
  cleanup_pending = boolean,
  game_result_known = boolean,
  invocation_started = boolean,
  invocation_exited = boolean,
  invocation_returned = boolean,
  callback_completed = boolean,
  game_result = integer,
  game_result_name = string,
  game_result_source = "activation_return" | "server_result" | "server_notification" | "",
  replacement_allowed = boolean,
  reason = string,
  command_handle = "ability_command:..." | nil,
  retained_command_handle = "ability_command:..." | nil,
  name = string | nil,
  target_mode = "none" | "selected" | "explicit" | "selected_fallback",
  target_fallback = "none" | "selected",
  fallback_used = boolean,
  fallback_reason = string | nil,
  requested_target_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  target_override_applied = boolean,
  target_restore_attempted = boolean,
  target_restore_succeeded = boolean
}

Use terminal to detect lifecycle completion and cleanup_pending to retain ownership until target cleanup finishes. Neither means the ability succeeded. activation_proven and acknowledged report positive start evidence.

dispatching means native dispatch is in progress. superseded is terminal: other work or a changed player/ability context overtook the command. A terminal submitted status can have activation_proven=false: Core observed submission, but has no start proof. Missing proof alone is not permission to replay it. Retained terminal receipts may acquire later outcome information.

game_result_known distinguishes a captured game result from missing data; use game_result_name for display. game_result_source distinguishes an immediate activation return from a later server result or notification. Invocation fields describe transport progress only: invocation_started records entry, invocation_exited records exit including exceptions, invocation_returned records a normal return, and callback_completed records completion of the owning callback. Target override/restore flags likewise describe target handling, rather than ability activation.

A finished receipt evicted from the 64-record command history returns known=true, terminal=true, state="expired", reason="command_history_expired". This releases ownership without inventing an activation or failure outcome; missing outcome flags on that tombstone are not negative gameplay evidence. An unrecognized handle remains unknown. Handles do not survive Core restart/load.

if pending_command then
  local status = gos.abilities.command_status(pending_command)
  if status.known and status.terminal and not status.cleanup_pending then
    pending_command = nil
  end
end

When replacement_allowed=true, submit a replacement with replace_command=status.command_handle. A successful replacement returns a new command handle. Only replace a command owned by this script instance: reading a known status or seeing replacement_allowed=true does not grant ownership of another script's command.

A known off-bar row can return invalid because requests currently require an on-bar ability and valid script/player context. The row is still usable. metadata_request_status belongs only to info(), not action_slots() rows. Retry pending requests on a later tick.

items.title: Ability Row
items.text:
gos.abilities.action_slots() returns a pure array of current on-bar rows. Use loadout().action_bar_available and action_bar_truncated to distinguish a coherent empty bar from missing/incomplete observations. gos.abilities.info(ability) returns one matching row, including a known off-bar row, or nil.

{
  name = string,
  name_source = "client" | "core",
  on_bar = boolean,
  ability_handle = "ability:..." | nil,
  activation_handle = "ability:..." | nil,
  slot_index = integer | nil,
  key_number = integer | nil,
  ready = boolean,
  submission_pending = boolean,
  has_cooldown_remaining = boolean,
  cooldown_remaining = number | nil,
  has_cooldown_duration = boolean,
  cooldown_duration = number | nil,
  has_current_charges = boolean,
  current_charges = integer | nil,
  has_max_charges = boolean,
  max_charges = integer | nil,
  has_resource_cost = boolean,
  resource_cost = number | nil,
  has_line_of_sight_requirement = boolean,
  line_of_sight_required = boolean | nil

items.title: gos.actor_names
items.text: Read a bounded, epoch-checked snapshot of retained actor names without live-unit lookup.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.actor_names(handles, epoch)

items.title: gos.actor_names(handles, epoch?)
items.text:
Read cached actor names inside an update callback, without resolving live units or requesting new names from the game.

handles must be a dense array of zero to 64 well-formed nonzero Core unit handles. Sparse arrays, non-array keys, wrong types, malformed handles, and extra arguments raise a Lua error. Duplicate handles are permitted and return one row for each requested position. epoch is an optional nonzero opaque actors:... string previously supplied by Core; malformed tokens raise an error. Omitting it requests the current store. Historical callers must supply the epoch saved with the handles, never the current epoch substituted later.

{
  status = "ready" | "epoch_mismatch" | "unavailable",
  epoch = "actors:..." | nil,
  revision = integer,
  items = {
    {
      handle = "unit:...",
      status = "ready" | "not_retained",
      revision = integer,
      name = string | nil
    }, ...
  }
}

A ready response is a complete snapshot in request order, including explicit not_retained rows. Names are nonempty UTF-8 strings no longer than 63 bytes. A missing record has no name and a record revision of zero. not_retained means the store does not currently retain a verified name: it may never have observed one or may have evicted it. It does not claim the actor is dead or that a saved name became invalid. Retention is bounded; eventual recovery is not promised. Previously delivered event/presentation strings remain usable.

An epoch_mismatch response contains no items and identifies the current epoch; do not retry the old handles with that epoch merely to obtain a name. An unavailable response also contains no items. A successful response's revision and rows belong to the same snapshot.

Each request returns its full result, including when the revision is unchanged. Use actor_revision from a world/event batch to skip redundant reads only after reading that exact handle set. A new set or chunk needs an initial read even at the same global revision. Record revisions order updates within one epoch. An older event name may fill an unnamed label but must not overwrite a newer metadata result.

local saved_handle, saved_epoch
local last_revision
local display_name

gos.on_tick(function()
  local world = gos.world()
  if not saved_handle and world.current_target and world.actor_epoch then
    saved_handle = world.current_target:handle()
    saved_epoch = world.actor_epoch
  end
  if not saved_handle or saved_epoch ~= world.actor_epoch then return end
  if last_revision == world.actor_revision then return end
  local snapshot = gos.actor_names({ saved_handle }, saved_epoch)
  if snapshot.status ~= "ready" then return end
  local row = snapshot.items[1]
  if row.status == "ready" then display_name = row.name end
  last_revision = snapshot.revision
  -- Retain display_name when the row is not_retained; do not invent a label.
end, { interval_ms = 250 })

This example tracks one actor for the captured epoch. Reset its saved handle, epoch and revision when choosing a different actor. Updating a label should not change event totals or order.

items.title: gos.events.combat
items.text: Consume ordered combat events using a retained cursor, with loss and backlog reporting.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.events.combat(cursor)

items.title: gos.events.combat(cursor?)
items.text:
Reads an ordered bounded event stream. Omit the cursor on the first call to subscribe at the current head, then pass the returned cursor on later calls.

local combat_cursor

gos.on_tick(function()
  local batch = gos.events.combat(combat_cursor)
  combat_cursor = batch.cursor

  for _, event in ipairs(batch.events) do
    -- Consume in order.
  end

  if batch.dropped > 0 then
    gos.log.warn("Combat events dropped", batch.dropped)
  end
end)

The cursor must be a non-negative integer or nil. Extra arguments, an invalid/future cursor, an unavailable stream, or a failed read raise a Lua error; they do not return a successful empty batch. Subscribe inside a tick callback, not while loading. Preserve the returned cursor exactly: filtered-out unknown events may advance it even when the returned array is empty.

Batch shape:

{
  cursor = integer,
  dropped = integer,
  more = boolean,
  actor_epoch = "actors:..." | nil,
  actor_revision = integer,
  events = { CombatEvent, ... }
}

Each call returns at most 64 events. If more=true, call again with the returned cursor on a later bounded pass. dropped reports records overwritten before a stale cursor could read them.

Event shape; fields other than kind are optional:

{
  kind = "damage" | "heal" | "ability" | "effect" |
         "resource" | "death" | "combat",
  action = string | nil,
  result = string | nil,
  source_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  target_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  source_name = string | nil,
  target_name = string | nil,
  actor_epoch = "actors:..." | nil,
  ability_handle = "ability:..." | nil,
  effect_handle = "effect:..." | nil,
  name = string | nil,
  amount = number | nil,
  effective_amount = number | nil,
  damage_type = string | nil,
  critical = boolean | nil,
  timestamp = integer | nil
}

name is not emitted for effect-kind events. Do not build buff-name matching around event.name; use the documented effect queries for current effect observations. Event timestamps are monotonic milliseconds, not Unix timestamps.

Actor names are optional, verified display labels for their respective handles. They are immutable event snapshots, not grouping keys. Separate actors with the same name must remain separate. Absence of a name never means absence of damage. The name authority is shared with unit:name() and gos.actor_names.

The batch's actor_epoch and actor_revision describe the current metadata store. Each event's actor_epoch describes its production session, which may be older than the batch when queued events cross a session transition. Never substitute the batch epoch for an event epoch. Preserve names already delivered with old events; do not enrich old handles using a newer epoch. Epoch tokens are opaque process-local strings, not identifiers to persist across Core reloads.

Use gos.actor_names(handles, epoch) for bounded late name updates without waiting for another combat event. It does not modify or replay existing events. Missing actor/effect metadata does not justify guessing a name from the ability.

Handles can still be resolved against the current world for live unit state when the unit is captured in the same actor epoch; historical labels do not require this lookup:

local world = gos.world()
local source = event.actor_epoch and event.actor_epoch == world.actor_epoch and
  event.source_handle and world:resolve(event.source_handle) or nil

items.title: gos.input.cursor
items.text: Read the current cursor in render-viewport pixels without capturing input; unavailable samples omit coordinates.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.input.cursor()

items.title: gos.input.cursor()
items.text:
Read the latest prepared cursor sample in render-viewport pixels inside gos.on_tick. This is a read-only query: it does not register an interaction rectangle, capture input, move the pointer, select a target, or cast an ability. It accepts no arguments; extra arguments, including an explicit nil, raise a Lua argument error.

{
  available = boolean,
  x = number | nil,
  y = number | nil,
  width = integer | nil,
  height = integer | nil
}

When available is true, x and y are cursor coordinates and width and height are the positive render-viewport dimensions. The origin is the top-left; X increases rightwards and Y increases downwards. Coordinates are in the same pixel space as unit screen anchors and screen-space overlay drawings, not desktop coordinates or game-world units. The cursor sample is quantized to whole pixels, returned as Lua numbers.

When unavailable, the result contains only { available = false }. All four coordinate/dimension fields are omitted; they are not zero-valued substitutes. This includes a missing render/input sample, no foreground game focus, a cursor outside the viewport, an open GoS menu, GoS text or hotkey capture, a GoS interaction rectangle under the pointer, or while either the left or right mouse button is held, including mouse-look drags. Read viewport size independently through gos.overlay.viewport() when cursor input is unavailable.

Availability is not a game-UI focus check. SWTOR chat, inventory and other native UI controls are not identified by this API. Reading the cursor or a key does not consume that key or prevent the game from acting on the same binding. An action hotkey therefore needs a deliberate input policy; do not treat available = true as permission to cast while typing in chat.

The sample is prepared by rendering; this call does not force a new input or projection update and does not promise that separate reads share a frame token. Do not reuse an earlier available sample to make a later gameplay decision after the current sample becomes unavailable.

This display-only example marks the current target when its projected center is within a 120-pixel cursor radius. It does not change the selected target.

gos.on_tick(function()
  if type(gos.input.cursor) ~= "function" then return end
  local cursor = gos.input.cursor()
  if not cursor.available then return end
  local world = gos.world()
  local unit = world and world.current_target
  if not unit or type(unit.screen_position) ~= "function" then return end
  local point = unit:screen_position("center")
  if not point then return end
  local dx, dy = point.x - cursor.x, point.y - cursor.y
  if dx * dx + dy * dy <= 120 * 120 then
    gos.overlay.draw_circle("cursor_target", {
      at = { screen = { x = point.x, y = point.y } },
      radius = 18, filled = false, frame = true,
    })
  end
end)

For nearest-unit selection, compare squared pixel distances across a bounded set of freshly captured, explicitly filtered units. Projection alone does not prove that a unit is alive, friendly, in ability range, in line of sight, or a legal ability target. Keep those checks separate from screen proximity. Older Core builds may not provide these two methods; the example checks their existence and takes no action when either is absent.

items.text: Read whether a supported keyboard or mouse button is held.

items.title: Signature

items.title: Key and button state
items.text:
gos.input.is_down(button)       -- boolean

gos.input.was_released(button)  -- boolean for this update
gos.input.state(button)         -- detailed table

state returns:

{
  name = string,
  virtual_key = integer,
  known = boolean,
  down = boolean,
  pressed = boolean,
  released = boolean
}

Buttons may be a canonical name, supported alias, integer virtual-key value in 1..255, decimal text, hexadecimal text, or vk:NN text. Canonical names include mouse1 through mouse5, common navigation/modifier keys, digits, letters, and f1 through f12. Unknown string names and out-of-range integer keys return false; state also sets known=false. Unsupported argument types such as a table, boolean or nil raise a Lua argument error instead of returning an unknown-button state.

Canonical single-digit strings are keyboard keys: "5" means the 5 key, not virtual-key value 5. Use "vk:5" or integer 5 for that numeric virtual key. Canonical names and aliases are case-insensitive.

Input edges are shared snapshot values and are not consumed by reading them.

Press/release edges belong to the current update; they are not accumulated separately for a throttled callback. A callback using interval_ms can miss an edge between its runs. items.title: gos.inventory.bag
items.text: Read occupied carried-bag slots and optional item metadata.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.inventory.bag()

items.title: Contract and usage
items.text: Read carried-bag and Materials storage snapshots during a tick. These queries do not change items and do not cover equipped gear or bank contents. All three functions take no arguments; extra arguments raise a Lua error. Repeated reads in one Lua tick use the same prepared snapshot, not an immediate client refresh. Tables can be retained as historical data, but are not live views.

items.title: gos.inventory.bag()
items.text:
Returns the bag subtable from the prepared inventory snapshot. Check status before reading any other field. pending and unavailable contain only status; they are not evidence of an empty bag. Only a ready table with used == 0 represents an observed empty bag.

{
  status = "ready", revision = integer,
  capacity = integer, used = integer, names_complete = boolean,
  items = {
    {
      slot = integer, handle = "item:...",
      prototype_handle = "item_prototype:...", prototype = string | nil,
      quantity = integer | nil, name = string | nil,
      name_source = "client" | "en_us_catalog" | nil,
      name_status = "pending" | "ready" | "unavailable",
      item_rating = integer | nil, item_level = integer | nil,
      enhanced_item_level = integer | nil, required_level = integer | nil,
      durability = integer | nil, max_durability = integer | nil,
      quality = string | nil, bound = boolean | nil,
      weapon_damage_min = number | nil, weapon_damage_max = number | nil,
      shield_chance_raw = number | nil, shield_absorb_raw = number | nil
    }, ...
  }
}

items is a dense Lua array of occupied slots, sorted by physical slot. Slots are one-based, but an array index is not the physical slot when there are empty spaces. used counts occupied slots, not the sum of item quantities. Handles are opaque identities, not addresses; neither item handle can be passed to world:resolve, which accepts unit handles only. Do not parse or construct them.

Optional metadata arrives independently. Missing quantity does not mean one; missing bound is unknown, whereas bound=false is an observed false value. names_complete means every occupied row has a name, not that all metadata is ready. A name may be localized by the client or supplied by the pinned English catalog; prototype is an identifier path, not a display-name substitute. quality is one of cheap, standard, premium, prototype, artifact, legendary, legacy, quest, currency, or moddable; unsupported values are omitted. The two shield fields are unnormalized client floats: do not interpret them as percentages or 0..1 ratios without separate evidence. Revisions identify changed prepared data, including metadata updates. Reset consumer caches across gos.world().session_generation changes; revisions are not an account-wide inventory history or a promise that an item still exists.

items.title: Contract and usage

items.title: gos.inventory.materials()
items.text:
Returns Materials storage, not a filtered copy of the carried bag. Before a ready observation the table contains only status="pending" or "unavailable". A ready result has revision and a dense items array; an empty ready array means the observed storage is empty.

{
  status = "ready", revision = integer,
  items = {
    { prototype_handle = "item_prototype:...", quantity = integer,
      prototype = string | nil, name = string | nil,
      name_source = "en_us_catalog" | nil }, ...
  }
}

The pinned English catalog can supply names and prototype paths even when the corresponding material definition is not loaded; an unmapped name remains absent. Material quantities are independent of carried bag quantities. Keep the bag and Materials revisions separate.

items.title: gos.log.debug
items.text: Write a debug-level message to this script's log.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.log.debug(...)

items.title: Find a script's output
items.text:
Press Insert to open Core, select the script in Scripts, and open Log. print and gos.log.info appear under INFO, including SUCCESS messages. DEBUG is off by default; turn it on for gos.log.debug. Keep ERROR on and clear Search logs when checking load or callback failures. Reload failed: above the log reports a failed load/reload; a callback error disables that callback until Reload.

Save exports the retained log and reports its path. The default filename is the script's stem plus .log.txt, beside the script. Folders > Lua log folder can change the destination. Saved files also include request diagnostics; review their contents before sharing an excerpt. Messages are retained in a bounded console buffer; do not assume every message is already saved to disk. For a complete first run, see Getting started.

items.title: Log messages
items.text:
print("Loaded")
gos.log.debug("State", state)
gos.log.info("Enabled")
gos.log.success("Command completed")
gos.log.warn("Event gap", dropped)
gos.log.error("Cannot continue", reason)

These helpers join arguments with spaces. The five gos.log convenience methods return boolean success. print(...) logs at info level and returns no values; do not use its return value as a success flag.

Messages are sanitized and limited to 1024 bytes; multibyte text can reach the limit in fewer characters. Each script has its own bounded log buffer.

items.title: gos.on_tick
items.text: Register bounded work on the update scheduler; optional interval_ms controls cadence.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.on_tick(callback, options)

items.title: gos.on_tick(callback, options?)
items.text:
Register while a script loads or from one of its active callbacks. Registration without a loaded-script owner raises a Lua error. Reloading creates a new script instance; old requests and click-intent tickets do not transfer to it.

Returns no values; callbacks receive no arguments. Only interval_ms is read from options. Unknown keys are ignored, so a misspelling leaves the default every-update cadence in effect.

Registers a function on Core's update scheduler. With no options it runs every worker update. options.interval_ms may request a lower cadence from 0 to 60000 milliseconds; a due callback never runs more than once per worker update.

gos.on_tick(function()
  local world = gos.world()
  if world.player then
    -- Read the current immutable snapshot here.
  end
end)

For visual callbacks, skipped interval ticks retain the callback's last frame-local overlay contribution. An unhandled error disables only the failing callback and removes that callback's frame-local contribution until scripts reload.

Callbacks should be bounded and non-blocking. The Release runtime accepts at most 256 registered callbacks.

items.title: gos.overlay.draw_bar
items.text: Draw a bounded bar at a shared screen, world or unit PointSpec.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.overlay.draw_bar(id, unit_or_options, options)

items.title: Contract and usage
items.text: Submit drawings and interaction regions from gos.on_tick. Every draw function returns a boolean indicating whether the submission was accepted.

items.title: gos.overlay.draw_bar(id, options)
items.text:
Requires positive width and height; clamps value to 0..1. Supports bg_color, border and border_color.

gos.overlay.draw_bar("health", {
  at = { unit = unit, anchor = "top",
         pixel_offset = { x = -45, y = -18 } },
  width = 90, height = 6,
  value = 0.5, color = "green",
  bg_color = { r = 12, g = 14, b = 16, a = 220 },
  border = true, border_color = "black",
})

items.title: PointSpec
items.text:
Every draw_* primitive accepts the same point format. One-point primitives use options.at; lines use options.from and options.to. Unit examples require a current unit from gos.world().

-- Exactly one base per point.
{ screen = { x = 100, y = 200 }, pixel_offset = { x = 0, y = 0 } }
{ world = { x = 1, y = 2, z = 3 }, pixel_offset = { x = 0, y = -10 } }
{
  unit = unit, -- or unit_handle = "unit:..."
  anchor = "origin", -- default for PointSpec units
  world_offset = { x = 0, y = 0.2, z = 0 },
  local_offset = { right = 0, up = 0, forward = 0 },
  pixel_offset = { x = 0, y = -24 },
}
{ unit = unit, anchor = "top" | "center" | "bottom",
  pixel_offset = { x = 0, y = -4 } }

World and local offsets use the same game-world units as unit:position(); 0.1 world unit is one metre. local_offset uses unit:basis() and requires current rotation. Box anchors, screen points and absolute-world points accept only pixel_offset.

Unit origins use the current render pose. World/local offsets are applied in 3D, projection uses the current camera, and pixel_offset is applied last. No screen-box fallback is substituted for a missing unit origin.

items.title: gos.overlay.interact
items.text: Refresh a screen interaction rectangle and read mouse interaction state.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.overlay.interact(id, rect)

items.title: Contract and usage
items.text: Submit drawings and interaction regions from gos.on_tick. Every draw function returns a boolean indicating whether the submission was accepted.

items.title: gos.overlay.interact(id, rect)
items.text:
Requires an active script callback. An empty or over-31-byte ID, an ID containing embedded zero bytes, an invalid rectangle, nonpositive TTL, or wrong arguments raise a Lua error. Drawing and interaction IDs use the same validation and are never truncated. Registers a temporary screen rectangle and returns left-mouse interaction:

local state = gos.overlay.interact("button", {
  x = 20, y = 20, width = 120, height = 28, ttl = 0.25,
})

-- state:
{
  hovered = boolean,
  pressed = boolean,
  down = boolean,
  released = boolean,
  clicked = boolean,
  mouse_x = number,
  mouse_y = number,
  entity_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  entity_generation = integer,
  entity_session_generation = integer,
  target_intent = userdata | nil
}

Refresh the rectangle before its TTL expires. A press retains capture through release. The Release snapshot retains at most 64 active interaction rectangles, with at most 40 contributed by one callback owner, subject to the 32-owner frame ceiling. If registration or input observation is unavailable, the result can contain all false flags and zero coordinates with no separate availability flag. That state alone is not proof that the pointer is outside the rectangle; stay within the published budgets.

For an entity-associated region, supply rect.entity = unit:handle() from the current world. This optional field accepts a Core unit-handle string, not a GosUnit; malformed values raise a Lua error. Omit it for ordinary UI buttons. The returned entity_handle is pinned on press, so a reordered list cannot turn the eventual click into a selection of the row's new occupant. Generation fields are zero when no entity observation exists.

entity_generation describes the displayed snapshot, not session identity. Resolve the returned handle in a fresh world and compare entity_session_generation to world.session_generation; ordinary tick changes must not invalidate a click. Do not use the row's current entity instead. For a completed entity click, target_intent is an immutable, script-owned ticket for gos.target.select. It can be absent when a click could not be authenticated. Do not manufacture a replacement or retry without it after rejection.

The following is a callback integration fragment; displayed_unit and the rectangle come from your current layout, while pending_target is retained by your script. It uses the pressed identity, not the layout's later contents:

local world = gos.world()
local state = gos.overlay.interact("ally_row", {
  x = 20, y = 60, width = 180, height = 28, ttl = 0.25,
  entity = displayed_unit:handle(),
})
if state.clicked and state.target_intent and state.entity_handle and
   state.entity_session_generation == world.session_generation then
  local clicked_unit = world:resolve(state.entity_handle)
  if clicked_unit then
    local ok, reason, handle = gos.target.select(clicked_unit, state.target_intent)
    if ok then pending_target = handle end
    -- Rejection is not permission to retry this click without its ticket.
  end
end

Poll any retained handle with gos.target.status in subsequent ticks; do not resubmit it on every update. See the target request contract for the two-second ticket window, native user-intent ordering, bounded receipt retention and cancellation limits. Rendering or registering a rectangle alone does not change the game's selected target.

local ok = gos.overlay.unit_label("focus", unit, {

items.title: gos.settings.get(script_id)
items.text:
Returns the current snapshot:

{
  script_id = string,
  title = string,
  version = integer,
  enabled = boolean,
  active = boolean,
  primary = boolean,
  activation = {
    mode = "always" | "hold" | "toggle" | "manual",

gos.on_tick(function()

items.title: gos.settings.register(script_id, schema)
items.text:
Registers a settings schema while the script loads and returns its current settings snapshot. Calling it from a tick callback raises an error.

local SCRIPT_ID = "example_rotation"

local Settings = gos.settings.register(SCRIPT_ID, {
  title = "Example Rotation",
  version = 1,
  activation = {
    mode = "hold",       -- always, hold, toggle, or manual
    label = "Rotation Key",
    default = "mouse4",
  },
  fields = {
    {
      key = "show_status",
      type = "bool",
      label = "Show status",
      tooltip = "Draw the current rotation state.",
      default = true,
    },
    {
      key = "hp_threshold",
      type = "int",
      label = "HP threshold",
      default = 50,
      min = 1,
      max = 100,
      step = 1,
    },
    {
      key = "mode",
      type = "select",
      label = "Mode",
      default = "Single target",
      options = { "Single target", "Area" },
    },
    {
      key = "accent",
      type = "color",
      label = "Accent",
      default = "#00CCFFFF",
    },
  },
})

Supported field types:

Type Lua value Relevant schema keys bool boolean default number number default, min, max, step int integer default, min, max, step string string default, max_length (maximum 256) select string default, options (1-32 strings) hotkey string default color string default as #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA

Every field requires key, type, label, and default. Optional tooltip text appears in the settings UI. A schema can contain at most 256 fields. activation.default applies only to hold and toggle modes. While enabled, always and manual are active continuously, hold follows the configured key, and toggle changes state on a press.

Hotkey fields and hold/toggle activation keys use an inline capture button: click it, then press a keyboard key or mouse button. Escape cancels capture, and left/right mouse buttons are ignored. Uncommon keys persist as vk:0xNN; the UI displays their current keyboard-layout name. Optional activation keys also expose a separate clear button.

Fields may also declare UI visibility gates:

{
  key = "telekinetics_option",
  type = "bool",
  label = "Telekinetics option",
  default = false,
  disciplines = { "Telekinetics" },
  requires_ability = "Telekinetic Gust",
}

disciplines matches exact display discipline names and requires_ability matches a key in gos.abilities.loadout().known. Both gates must match when both are present. These gates affect settings visibility only; scripts must still validate their active loadout before using the setting.

Core shows gated rows while loadout identity is still pending or unavailable, then hides nonmatching rows once the loadout is ready. Validated values and activation keys persist across reloads.

items.text:
Queues a validated setting update from a running tick:

items.title: gos.target.cancel(request_handle)
items.text:
Requests cancellation of this script's still-queued selection request. Returns the same status shape as gos.target.status, with an additional ok boolean. ok=true confirms successful cancellation before invocation; ok=false may mean dispatch already began, the request is terminal, it is not owned by this script, or the handle is unknown. Inspect the returned state. Cancellation does not undo a selection that already happened and does not stop dispatched work. A failed cancellation is not permission to forget or replay a pending request.

items.title: gos.target.select
items.text: Request an intentional persistent selected-target change; confirm it in a later snapshot.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.target.select(unit, target_intent)

items.title: gos.target.select(unit, target_intent?)
items.text:
Requests a persistent selected-target change for a current-generation non-object GosUnit. Keep the optional third return value to observe the request:

local ok, error, request_handle = gos.target.select(ally)

true, nil, handle means a request was accepted, not that selection occurred. true, nil, nil normally means the current snapshot already selects that unit. The handle is an opaque string, distinct from a unit or ability-command handle. Poll gos.target.status(handle) on later ticks instead of submitting every tick.

Operational failures return false, reason, nil, with busy, invalid_target, stale_world, stale_intent, request_capacity, or unavailable. Wrong argument types and stale userdata raise Lua errors (stale_unit for expired units). Only one or two arguments are accepted. Omitted/nil target_intent remains supported for intentional script-driven selection.

For a captured overlay click, pass the immutable state.target_intent ticket from gos.overlay.interact. It is bound to the submitting script instance, pressed entity and session. Another entity/session/script, a newer native user selection, or a ticket at least two seconds old produces stale_intent. Repeating a still-valid ticket returns its retained receipt rather than replaying the click. Never replace a rejected ticket with a ticketless retry.

Queued requests have a two-second dispatch/observation window, measured from the click for a ticket or from submission otherwise. Busy shared work can defer progress. A newer request can supersede this script's still-cancellable queued request; it does not cancel another script's dispatched work. Capacity is bounded to 64 retained target requests. The deadline does not forcibly stop running work.

Selection persists and is separate from explicit ability targeting: default explicit casts do not call this API or persistently change the selected target. See gos.target.status for confirmation and gos.target.cancel for safe queued cancellation.

See also: gos.target.status(request_handle) | gos.target.cancel(request_handle)

items.title: gos.target.status
items.text: Observe an owned target-selection request without replaying it.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.target.status(request_handle)

items.title: gos.target.status(request_handle)
items.text:
Reads this script instance's retained request without changing selection. Use the opaque string returned by gos.target.select. Malformed strings, unknown/evicted requests, and requests owned by another script report known=false, terminal=true, state="unknown"; they are not success receipts. A non-string argument can raise a Lua argument error.

{
  known = boolean, terminal = boolean,
  state = "unknown" | "queued" | "dispatched" | "observed" |
          "expired" | "cancelled" | "superseded" | "failed" | "unconfirmed",
  request_handle = string | nil, target_handle = "unit:..." | nil,
  invocation_returned = boolean, callback_completed = boolean,
  blocker = table | nil
}

queued and dispatched are nonterminal. observed means a later prepared selection matched this request's target and session within its observation window. It does not promise the target is still selected now. expired means the queued request expired before dispatch; cancelled and superseded describe successfully retired queued intent. failed reports a pre-invocation failure. unconfirmed means the request may have taken effect but confirmation is missing, including a completed invocation without an in-window matching observation or a session change. Do not equate it with cancellation or automatically replay it.

invocation_returned and callback_completed describe invocation progress, not selection proof. A dispatched request is not forcibly interrupted when its deadline passes. blocker is optional diagnostic-only metadata: its internal keys and numeric values are not a stable scripting contract. Branch on the public state, not those internals. Receipts have bounded retention; save only the result information your UI needs, and do not carry requests across reloads.

See also: gos.target.select(unit, target_intent?) | gos.target.cancel(request_handle)

items.text: Acquire the current generation-bound world and its optional player and target.

items.title: Signature
items.text: gos.world()

items.title: gos.world()
items.text:
Returns the current generation-bound world:

{
  generation = integer,
  session_generation = integer,
  actor_epoch = "actors:..." | nil,
  actor_revision = integer | nil,
  player = GosUnit | nil,
  current_target = GosUnit | nil,
  units = function,
  resolve = function,
  presence = function
}

player is the local player. current_target is the currently captured target. Either may be nil when unavailable. actor_epoch is the stable metadata-session token, not the per-tick generation. actor_revision changes when retained actor name metadata changes; ordinary unit movement does not change it. Both metadata fields are omitted when the actor-name authority is unavailable.

generation identifies one prepared snapshot and can change every tick. session_generation instead identifies the Core session and remains stable across ordinary ticks. It is zero when no combat snapshot is available. Use the session value to reject interactions saved from another session; do not reject a valid click merely because its snapshot generation differs from this tick. Neither field makes an old GosUnit current: resolve saved handles again.

items.title: Unit Identity And Lifetime
items.text:
Every GosUnit state-reading method raises stale_unit after its world generation expires. unit:handle() is the exception and remains available so the unit can be reacquired with a fresh world:resolve(handle).

Within one world, repeated lookups of the same unit compare equal with ==. Values from different generations compare unequal even when their handles match.

items.title: Signature

items.title: Find a script's output
items.text:
Press Insert to open Core, select the script in Scripts, and open Log. print and gos.log.info appear under INFO, including SUCCESS messages. DEBUG is off by default; turn it on for gos.log.debug. Keep ERROR on and clear Search logs when checking load or callback failures. Reload failed: above the log reports a failed load/reload; a callback error disables that callback until Reload.

Save exports the retained log and reports its path. The default filename is the script's stem plus .log.txt, beside the script. Folders > Lua log folder can change the destination. For a complete first run, see Getting started.

items.title: Log messages
items.text:
print("Loaded")
gos.log.debug("State", state)
gos.log.info("Enabled")
gos.log.success("Command completed")
gos.log.warn("Event gap", dropped)
gos.log.error("Cannot continue", reason)

These helpers join arguments with spaces. The five gos.log convenience methods return boolean success. print(...) logs at info level and returns no values; do not use its return value as a success flag.

Messages are sanitized and limited to 1024 bytes; multibyte text can reach the limit in fewer characters. Each script has its own bounded log buffer.

items.title: unit:effect
items.text: Query a named or definition-key-matched aggregate; check readiness and completeness.

items.title: Signature
items.text: unit:effect(name, options)

items.title: Contract and usage
items.text:
Resolve the unit in the current world before querying it. A stale unit raises a Lua stale_unit error; this is distinct from a current unit returning a pending or unavailable effect observation.

Queries return the latest completed poll, rather than reading effects synchronously. A ready sample remains usable while its refresh is queued; applications/removals appear at the next publication. Timers age from the original sample between polls.

Check status and completeness. A complete ready observation establishes presence/absence as of that poll. Pending or unavailable data is not an empty effect list.

items.title: unit:effect(name, options?)
items.text:
Returns one case-insensitive named aggregate:

{
  status = "ready" | "pending" | "unavailable",
  reason = string,
  age_ms = integer | nil,
  truncated = boolean,

  -- Present only when status == "ready":
  present = boolean | nil,
  has_charges = boolean | nil,
  charge_conflicted = boolean | nil,
  stacks = integer | nil,
  has_timer = boolean | nil,
  remaining = number | nil,
  kind = "buff" | "debuff" | "passive" | "other" | "none" | nil,
  has_ownership = boolean | nil,
  mine = boolean | nil
}

Options:

local proc = player:effect("Tidal Force", {
  kind = "buff",       -- any, buff, debuff, passive, or other
  timed = true,         -- require or reject a timer
  charged = false,      -- require or reject a charge observation
})

if proc.status == "ready" and proc.present then
  local remaining = proc.has_timer and proc.remaining or nil
end

The singular query prefers exact local-player-owned rows when local and foreign effects share a name. mine is output metadata, not a filter. A truncated scan that cannot prove absence returns an unavailable result rather than present=false.

Omitted options impose no kind, timer, or charge filter. Supplied filters combine with AND; unknown keys and wrong filter types raise a Lua error. charged=true includes conflicted charge observations, so it does not guarantee a usable stacks value. Require has_charges=true and charge_conflicted=false before making a stack-count decision. remaining and duration use seconds; age_ms and last_known_age_ms use milliseconds.

has_ownership=false means source identity is unavailable; mine=false alone does not establish foreign ownership. Kind follows the observed effect classification; an absent timer or an Other list does not prove an effect is passive.

Common public reasons are none, observation_pending, unsupported_unit, observation_capacity, and not_captured. Treat other reasons as diagnostics: branch on status rather than undocumented reason strings.

items.title: Exact effect identity
items.text:
definition_key identifies an effect definition, not an effect instance, a unit, or a castable ability. Same-name variants can have different keys. Treat keys as opaque and use an observed value; do not manufacture one. A key never makes a pending or historical row current. Both query forms accept a definition_key filter. To query only by key, pass an empty name to unit:effect("", { definition_key = observed_key }).

Plural rows expose has_duration and, when available, total duration in seconds. Duration is independent of remaining; do not estimate it from the first timer value you happen to see.

  last_known_age_ms = integer | nil,
  truncated = boolean,
  last_known_truncated = boolean,
  items = { EffectRow, ... },
  last_known_items = { EffectRow, ... }
}

Both arrays use this row shape:

{
  definition_key = "effectdef:<16 uppercase hex digits>" | nil,
  name = string,
  name_source = "client" | "core",
  freshness = "current" | "last_known",
  has_charges = boolean,
  charge_conflicted = boolean,
  stacks = integer | nil,
  has_timer = boolean,
  remaining = number | nil,
  has_duration = boolean,
  duration = number | nil,
  kind = "buff" | "debuff" | "passive" | "other",

local debuffs = target:effects({ kind = "debuff", timed = true })

  for _, effect in ipairs(debuffs.items) do
    if effect.mine then
      gos.log.debug(effect.name, effect.remaining or "untimed")
    end
  end
end

items.title: Exact effect identity
items.text:
definition_key identifies an effect definition, not an effect instance, a unit, or a castable ability. Same-name variants can have different keys. Plural rows expose has_duration and, when available, total duration in seconds. Duration is independent of remaining; do not estimate it from the first timer value you happen to see.

items.title: unit:screen_position(anchor?)
items.text:
Read a projected anchor from this unit's current, generation-validated render observation. This method reads prepared screen coordinates; it does not perform a world-to-screen calculation on demand, a screen-to-world raycast, or a line-of-sight test.

anchor is an optional lowercase string:

Anchor Point returned "top" Top-center of the prepared unit box "center" Vertical midpoint of the prepared unit box; the default "bottom" Bottom-center of the prepared unit box

Omitting the argument or passing nil uses "center". Unsupported anchor strings, non-string non-nil values, or extra arguments raise a Lua error. "middle" and "screen" are not accepted aliases for this method.

{ x = number, y = number } | nil

The returned X and Y are render-viewport pixels, with the origin at the top-left, X increasing rightwards and Y increasing downwards. They share the coordinate space of gos.input.cursor() and screen overlays. They are not the game-world coordinates returned by unit:position(), and no world-unit-to-metre conversion applies. These are box anchors, not anatomical bones or an exact clickable outline. Values are not clamped to the viewport.

Return nil when the current observation is not on screen or the prepared projection is unavailable/invalid. Do not reuse last-known pixels as a current targeting observation. An expired GosUnit raises stale_unit rather than returning nil; reacquire the unit from the current world before reading it.

gos.on_tick(function()
  local world = gos.world()
  local unit = world and world.current_target
  if not unit or type(unit.screen_position) ~= "function" then return end
  local point = unit:screen_position() -- default center
  if not point then return end
  gos.overlay.draw_circle("unit_anchor", {
    at = { screen = { x = point.x, y = point.y } },
    radius = 12, filled = false, frame = true,
  })
end)

A non-nil point proves only that these screen coordinates are available. Check health, reaction, range and native ability admission separately before acting. The method does not capture mouse input, change selection or cast anything, and can return a position even when the cursor query is unavailable. See the cursor example for a pixel-radius comparison.

items.text:
Reads prepared character-roster membership independently of camera projection. Pass a well-formed nonzero opaque unit handle; malformed handles raise a Lua error. This is a snapshot read, not a new world scan.

{
  state = "present" | "absent" | "unknown",
  complete = boolean,
  revision = integer,
  session_generation = integer,
  sample_ms = integer | nil
}

present means the identity appeared in the raw character roster. absent means a recently observed identity disappeared from a later complete capture. An untracked identity is unknown, even when complete is true. Neither absent nor a failed world:resolve establishes stealth, death, or cast legality. Objects and synthetic selected-target entries do not establish roster membership.

Evidence has a bounded 250 ms window: stale, incomplete, failed, or mismatched session captures return complete = false and state = "unknown". Recently departed identities also expire out of the retained history, becoming unknown. revision counts Core captures, not Lua callbacks; repeated calls at one revision are not independent disappearance observations. sample_ms is the monotonic capture timestamp in milliseconds, omitted before any capture. Retain the session with a saved handle and reject old-session evidence.

items.title: Write your own bounded Lua module
items.text:
A plain Lua ring buffer, independent of any GoS API. Save as bounded_history.lua in the shared module root and use require("bounded_history") from a script. Store copied records or handles, not generation-bound units. Do not mutate the buffer inside its each callback. This is a module, not an entry-point script to enable.

Download the module source and save it as bounded_history.lua under the actual COMMON_PATH shown by the status panel's Log tab. Click Reload after adding it so entry scripts can load the module.

items.title: Complete code
items.text:
local History = {}
History.__index = History
function History.new(capacity)
  assert(type(capacity) == "number" and capacity % 1 == 0
      and capacity >= 1 and capacity <= 4096, "capacity must be 1..4096")
  return setmetatable({ capacity = capacity, count = 0, next = 1, rows = {} }, History)
end
function History:push(value)
  assert(value ~= nil, "history value cannot be nil")
  self.rows[self.next] = value
  self.next = self.next % self.capacity + 1
  self.count = math.min(self.count + 1, self.capacity)
end
function History:each(callback)
  local start = self.count == self.capacity and self.next or 1
  for offset = 0, self.count - 1 do
    callback(self.rows[(start + offset - 1) % self.capacity + 1])
  end
end
return History

items.title: Bounded incoming damage counter
items.text:
Count damage reported against your character from the moment the script starts listening. The display also shows lost records, so you can tell when the total is incomplete.

The total is the sum of event.amount. It resets when disabled or when the player or session changes. Each update reads at most 256 events and accepts only those matching the player's handle and session.

Download incoming-damage.lua and follow the first-script installation steps. No helper modules are required.

items.title: Complete code
items.text:
local ID = "example_incoming_damage"
gos.settings.register(ID, {
  title = "Example: Incoming Damage", version = 1,
  activation = { mode = "always" }, fields = {},
})
local cursor, owner, epoch
local total, samples, dropped = 0, 0, 0
local MAX_BATCHES = 4

gos.on_tick(function()
  local settings = gos.settings.get(ID)
  local world = gos.world()
  local player = world.player
  local handle = player and player:handle() or nil
  if not settings.enabled or not settings.active or not handle or not world.actor_epoch then
    cursor, owner, epoch = nil, nil, nil
    total, samples, dropped = 0, 0, 0
    return
  end
  if handle ~= owner or world.actor_epoch ~= epoch then
    owner, epoch, cursor = handle, world.actor_epoch, nil
    total, samples, dropped = 0, 0, 0
  end
  for _ = 1, MAX_BATCHES do
    local batch = gos.events.combat(cursor)
    cursor = batch.cursor
    dropped = dropped + batch.dropped
    for _, event in ipairs(batch.events) do
      if event.kind == "damage" and event.actor_epoch == epoch and event.target_handle == handle
          and type(event.amount) == "number" then
        total = total + event.amount
        samples = samples + 1
      end
    end
    if not batch.more then break end
  end
  gos.overlay.draw_text("example_damage", {
    at = { screen = { x = 30, y = 110 } }, frame = true,
    text = string.format("Taken %.0f | hits %d | lost %d", total, samples, dropped),
    color = dropped > 0 and "orange" or "white", font_size = 16,
  })
end, { interval_ms = 100 })

items.title: Commando: when to use Supercharge
items.text:
Supercharged Kolto Cell resets Advanced Medical Probe (AMP) and restores ten energy cells. The script checks whether that reset will let it heal again, and whether it can afford the next heal. Reaching ten stacks alone is not enough.

Source: commando/combat_medic.lua in the official Commando / Mercenary package. Bodyguard uses the same decisions with Healing Scan and Supercharged Kolto Gas.
path: Commando and Mercenary Lua Healing Routine - Supercharge

items.title: Use the heal before resetting it
items.text:
If AMP is ready and someone needs it, cast AMP first. Once its cooldown appears, use Cell to reset it. This gets a heal from the ready ability before spending the reset.

If AMP is ready but energy is too low, Cell can go first when its ten cells make AMP affordable. The script also checks that enough energy will remain after the heal. For example, with a 100-cell maximum, a 20-cell heal and a 30-cell reserve, starting at 45 cells is enough: Cell raises it to 55, and the heal leaves 35.

The script waits for the healing GCD to finish before using Cell, so the buff does not start while the next heal is still blocked. It also checks movement and the chosen ally before spending the stacks.
path: Commando and Mercenary Lua Healing Routine - Supercharge

items.title: Build the last stacks with a useful heal
items.text:
While AMP is on cooldown, the script looks for a heal that can finish the stack count:

Current state What it tries Eight stacks and Potent Medicine learned Medical Probe for the last two stacks Nine stacks, with no need for a stronger direct heal Med Shot for the last stack Six to eight stacks and SC-4 Treatment Scanner active Successive Treatment to build stacks during a needed channel

Medical Probe still follows its setting for use above the direct-heal HP limit. The builder must be useful to someone who needs healing, and the script must have energy for both the builder and the AMP after Cell. Urgent healing comes first. Cell waits until ten stacks are actually observed, even when a channel is expected to produce them.
path: Commando and Mercenary Lua Healing Routine - Supercharge

items.title: The energy check and builder choice
items.text:
The first block checks energy after Cell and AMP. The second chooses a stack-building heal and includes its cost in the same calculation. Mercenary heat is converted to available energy with max - current before these checks.

Code from the class script

These extracts use the settings, current patient rows and helper functions in commando/combat_medic.lua. Use the full class package to run the rotation.

local after_refund=math.min(resource.max,resource.current+10)
local reserve=reserve_for(recipient)
if recipient.isSelf and hard_self then
    reserve=math.min(healing_reserve(recipient,cfg),cfg.critical_floor)
end
if after_refund<amp.cost or (after_refund-amp.cost)/resource.max*100<reserve then
    return nil,"insufficient_energy_for_amp_window"
end

stack_builder_plan=function()
    if not cfg.supercharge or support~=false or gcd>0 or hard_self or not healing_observation.complete then return nil,nil,"scheduler_guard" end
    local recipient=rows[1]
    if not recipient or triage_band(recipient,cfg)<2 or recipient.hp>cfg.focused_hp or skips[recipient.handle] then return nil,nil,"recipient_not_routine_or_needed" end
    local name,reason
    if supercharge_stacks==8 and learned(loadout,"Potent Medicine") then
        if recipient.hp>cfg.direct_hp and not cfg.medical_probe_bridge then return nil,nil,"probe_bridge_disabled" end
        name,reason="Medical Probe","amp_stack_completion"
    elseif supercharge_stacks==9 and recipient.hp>cfg.direct_hp then
        name,reason="Med Shot","amp_stack_completion"
    elseif sc4==true and type(supercharge_stacks)=="number" and
        supercharge_stacks>=6 and supercharge_stacks<=8 then
        -- SC-4 can supply the current 2-4 stack deficit during a useful
        -- Treatment channel. The plan never credits those stacks early.
        name,reason="Successive Treatment","sc4_stack_builder"
    else return nil,nil,"no_single_builder" end
    local amp=metadata("Advanced Medical Probe")
    local builder=metadata(name)
    if not amp or not amp_on_cooldown(amp.info) or not builder or not metadata("Supercharged Kolto Cell") or
        not movable("Advanced Medical Probe",amp.spec) or not movable(name,builder.spec) or not energy_known then return nil,nil,"ability_cooldown_mobility_or_energy_unknown" end
    -- Budget both actions using observed costs and the authored Cell
    -- refund. No predicted regeneration, crit refund, SC-4 stack credit,
    -- or extra Field Triage discount is used for admission.
    local after_refund=math.min(resource.max,resource.current-builder.cost+10)
    if after_refund<amp.cost or (after_refund-amp.cost)/resource.max*100<reserve_for(recipient) then return nil,nil,"followup_energy_budget" end
    local advice=amp_target_advice(recipient)
    if not advice or (advice.ok~=true and advice.reason~="cooldown" and advice.reason~="insufficient_resource") then return nil,nil,"amp_native_admission" end
    return name,recipient,reason
end

Before AMP is sent, the script checks its current cost and whether Core will allow the cast. The energy calculation above does not change the observed resource value.

items.title: Operative: cursor Holotraverse
items.text:
Aim near a character to choose a Holotraverse destination. The script picks the eligible character closest to your cursor, using their body center on screen. They must also be within the ability's 30-metre range.

Source: operative/cursor_holotraverse.lua, in the official Operative / Scoundrel package. Its mirror maps Holotraverse to Trick Move.
path: Operative Lua Addon Example - Cursor Holotraverse

items.title: Choose the nearest eligible body center
items.text:
The candidate must be alive, on screen, within range, and match an exact player/NPC/companion and reaction filter. Unknown health, distance or classification rejects it. Projection alone does not establish line of sight.

For example, a character 18 pixels from the cursor beats one 42 pixels away even if the latter is closer in world space. The default circle is 120 pixels. Equal distances use a stable handle tie-breaker.

Code from the class script

Keep the module's M table, MAX_UNITS = 512, MAX_RANGE_METERS = 30, METERS_PER_WORLD_UNIT = 10, and finite, method, alive, M.matches helpers. Those helpers validate numbers, call unit methods, check living HP and apply exact filters. The two functions below return copied scalar data rather than retaining units.
path: Operative Lua Addon Example - Cursor Holotraverse

items.title: Picker
items.text:
local function eligible(unit,player,filter)
    if unit==nil then return false,"target_unresolved" end
    if unit==player then return false,"self_target" end
    local is_local=method(unit,"is_local_player")
    if is_local~=false then return false,"local_player_flag_not_false" end
    if not alive(unit) then
        local hp=method(unit,"hp")
        local dead=type(hp)=="table" and finite(hp.current) and hp.current<=0
        return false,dead and "target_dead" or "target_hp_unavailable_or_invalid"
    end
    if not M.matches(filter,method(unit,"type"),method(unit,"reaction")) then
        return false,"target_filter_mismatch"
    end
    if method(unit,"is_on_screen")~=true then return false,"target_not_projected" end
    -- Native distance is the same game-world unit used by the existing routes.
    local distance=method(unit,"distance")
    if not finite(distance) or distance<0 then return false,"target_distance_unavailable" end
    if distance*METERS_PER_WORLD_UNIT>MAX_RANGE_METERS then return false,"target_out_of_range" end
    return true,"eligible"
end

function M.pick(world,cursor,filter,radius,counts)
    if not world or not world.player or not cursor or cursor.available~=true or
        not finite(cursor.x) or not finite(cursor.y) or not finite(cursor.width) or not finite(cursor.height) or
        cursor.width<=0 or cursor.height<=0 or not finite(radius) or radius<=0 then
        return nil,"cursor_unavailable"
    end
    local units=method(world,"units")
    if type(units)~="table" or #units>MAX_UNITS then return nil,"world_unavailable" end
    local best,limit=nil,radius*radius
    if counts then
        counts.total,counts.eligible,counts.range,counts.projection,counts.other,counts.outside = #units,0,0,0,0,0
        counts.nearest_px=nil
    end
    for _,unit in ipairs(units) do
        local allowed,gate=eligible(unit,world.player,filter)
        if counts and not allowed then
            if gate=="target_out_of_range" then counts.range=counts.range+1
            elseif gate=="target_not_projected" then counts.projection=counts.projection+1
            else counts.other=counts.other+1 end
        end
        if allowed then
            if counts then counts.eligible=counts.eligible+1 end
            local pos=method(unit,"screen_position","center")
            local handle=method(unit,"handle")
            if type(pos)=="table" and finite(pos.x) and finite(pos.y) and type(handle)=="string" and
                pos.x>=0 and pos.y>=0 and pos.x<cursor.width and pos.y<cursor.height then
                local dx,dy=pos.x-cursor.x,pos.y-cursor.y
                local d2=dx*dx+dy*dy
                if counts then
                    local pixels=math.sqrt(d2)
                    counts.nearest_px=math.min(counts.nearest_px or pixels,pixels)
                    if d2>limit then counts.outside=counts.outside+1 end
                end
                if d2<=limit and (not best or d2<best.d2 or (d2==best.d2 and handle<best.handle)) then
                    best={handle=handle,d2=d2,x=pos.x,y=pos.y}
                end
            elseif counts then
                counts.projection=counts.projection+1
            end
        end
    end
    return best,best and "candidate" or "no_target_in_cursor_radius"
end
path: Operative Lua Addon Example - Cursor Holotraverse

items.title: Use the result
items.text:
Call M.pick(world, gos.input.cursor(), "All", 120) with a fresh world = gos.world(). It returns {handle, d2, x, y} and a reason, or nil if nobody qualifies. d2 is squared pixel distance; optional counts records why candidates were rejected. The scan stops if cursor data is missing or the list has more than 512 units.

The full script scans at most once per 50 ms. Before casting, it finds the chosen character again and checks that they are still valid. It uses target_fallback = "none" so a missing destination cannot redirect the cast to the selected target.

Hold Shift+V to keep trying, including while waiting for cooldown. Releasing either key stops new requests; one already sent may still finish. While held, the script waits for each command to finish before choosing another destination.

items.title: Operative: maintain Kolto Probe stacks
items.text:
Keep two Kolto Probe stacks on an ally and refresh them before they expire. This helper says whether another Probe is needed. The class script handles urgent healing first and checks whether it can cast.

Source: operative/medicine.lua, in the official Operative / Scoundrel package.

Code from the class script

Requires mine_effect_snapshot, finite_number, KOLTO_PROBE, KOLTO_PROBE_MAX_STACKS, and policy.koltoProbeRefreshSeconds. The snapshot is nil when unresolved, otherwise a table with stacks and optional remaining in seconds. Resolve an eligible ally from the current world before calling it.
path: Operative Medicine Lua Healing - Kolto Probe Stacks

items.title: Refresh decision
items.text:
local function kolto_probe_needs_refresh(unit, policy)
    local state = mine_effect_snapshot(unit, KOLTO_PROBE, "buff")
    -- Unknown observation is not evidence that the HoT is missing; fail closed
    -- so the route cannot spam Kolto Probe while Core catches up.
    if state == nil then return false, "observation_unknown" end
    if state.stacks < KOLTO_PROBE_MAX_STACKS then
        return true, "build_" .. tostring(state.stacks + 1)
    end
    if finite_number(state.remaining) and
        state.remaining <= policy.koltoProbeRefreshSeconds then
        return true, "refresh_expiring"
    end
    return false, "healthy"
end

build_1 and build_2 mean a stack is needed. refresh_expiring means the remaining time is below the chosen refresh setting. healthy means no refresh is needed. If the buff cannot be read, observation_unknown stops the helper from repeatedly asking for Probe. A missing timer does not mean the buff has expired.
path: Operative Medicine Lua Healing - Kolto Probe Stacks

items.title: Check ownership when reusing this
items.text:
The source helper treats mine ~= true as zero owned stacks. It counts a present owned HoT as one stack if the stack count is unknown. Those choices affect when it asks for another Probe; observation_unknown only covers cases where the helper returns nil.

For a general HoT tracker, require has_ownership before treating a row as foreign and preserve unknown charge counts. mine = false alone does not prove another player owns the HoT.

items.title: Sage: Presence of Mind and proc prediction
items.text: Sage predicts when Presence of Mind should update and tracks the events that grant Tidal Force. This lets it prepare the next spell while waiting for the buff snapshot. It tracks which proc is already being used to avoid submitting the same spell twice.
path: Sage Lua Combat Routine - Presence of Mind and Proc Prediction

items.title: Presence of Mind: learn the Throw tick timing
items.text:
The PoM example comes from sage/balance.lua in the official Sage / Sorcerer package. The Sorcerer version uses Wrath and Force Lightning.

The script records when Telekinetic Throw starts and when its damage ticks arrive. After two ticks, it calculates their average spacing:

tick interval = (latest tick time - first tick time) / (tick count - 1)

It adds that interval to the latest tick time to estimate the next one. For ticks at 1000 ms and 1450 ms, the next estimate is 1900 ms. With only one tick, it uses the spacing learned from earlier channels when available.

Time passing does not add a stack. When the starting stacks plus received Throw ticks reach four, the script waits for the PoM buff update instead of starting filler. The next spell still requires four observed stacks.
path: Sage Lua Combat Routine - Presence of Mind and Proc Prediction

items.title: Check the buff before spending it
items.text:
A buff snapshot may predate the damage tick. The script uses the snapshot's age to tell whether a lower stack count is old information. A lower count sampled at least two milliseconds after the tick cancels the expectation; the small margin avoids rounding errors in the timestamps.

Once the next spell has been submitted, late Throw ticks cannot make the script spend the same proc again. An interrupted channel or missing combat records clears the pending expectation.

Code from the class script

These extracts show the next-tick calculation and the observed-stack check in sage/balance.lua. They use that script's channel state, validated buff data and PRESENCE_MAX_STACKS = 4; the event reader and cast handling stay in the full package. Times in the first block are milliseconds.

local next_interval_ms = nil
if presence_throw_tick_count >= 2 and
    type(presence_throw_first_tick_ms) == "number" and
    event.timestamp > presence_throw_first_tick_ms then
    next_interval_ms =
        (event.timestamp - presence_throw_first_tick_ms) /
        (presence_throw_tick_count - 1)
elseif type(presence_tick_interval_mean_ms) == "number" then
    next_interval_ms = presence_tick_interval_mean_ms
end
presence_throw_predicted_next_tick_ms =
    type(next_interval_ms) == "number" and
    event.timestamp + next_interval_ms or nil

local function observed_presence_stacks(state)
    local presence = state.effects.presenceOfMind
    return presence.present and
        type(presence.stacks) == "number" and presence.stacks or 0
end

local function presence_projection(state)
    local observed = observed_presence_stacks(state)
    if observed >= PRESENCE_MAX_STACKS then
        return true, observed, "observed"
    end
    return false, observed, "observed"
end
path: Sage Lua Combat Routine - Presence of Mind and Proc Prediction

items.title: Telekinetics: Tidal Force uses the same kind of evidence
items.text:
This approach is useful beyond Balance. In sage/telekinetics.lua, the script watches Forcequake starting and events where spells such as Turbulence spend Force. It also tracks when Tidal Force's internal cooldown ends. When a matching event arrives after that cooldown, it can prepare Telekinetic Wave before the buff snapshot catches up.

Unlike the PoM check above, that exact Tidal Force event can authorize the next spell. The script marks the proc as claimed when Wave is submitted, then checks whether the cast actually started before deciding if it can be used again. It matches the later buff observation to the event record and keeps the proc claimed while Wave is pending.

items.title: Seer: predict who needs healing next
items.text:
An ally at 80% HP can be closer to death than one at 50%. Seer estimates how fast each ally is losing health, accounts for healing over time, and predicts their health two and four seconds ahead. It also estimates seconds until death if that damage continues.

Source: combat/pressure_formula.lua, used through combat/pressure_tracker.lua by sage/seer.lua in the official Sage / Sorcerer package.
path: Sage Seer Lua Healing Routine - Predictive Triage

items.title: Measure damage over three periods
items.text:
The tracker groups recent damage into separate periods so the same hit is counted once. It divides each total by maximum HP and the period's length to get health lost per second.

How long ago the damage happened Weight for the two-second estimate Weight for the four-second estimate Up to 0.75 seconds 45% 15% 0.75 to 2 seconds 35% 45% 2 to 4 seconds 20% 40%

The formula gives more weight to attackers who keep hitting the same ally. recent_attackers hit within the last 0.75 seconds; persistent_attackers also hit in an older period. This helps distinguish a single spike from continuing damage.
path: Sage Seer Lua Healing Routine - Predictive Triage

items.title: Estimate health and time to death
items.text:
fast_pressure and slow_pressure are the estimated fractions of maximum HP lost per second. The formula subtracts that damage from current health and adds part of the expected healing over time: 80% for the two-second estimate and 70% for the four-second estimate.

Time to death = current health fraction / net health lost per second. Net loss subtracts the expected healing rate from the damage rate. The 0.001 minimum keeps the division finite; a large result means little or no continuing danger in this model.

For example, at 80% HP with an estimated loss of 40% of maximum HP per second and no healing over time, the result is two seconds until death. That ally can move ahead of a stable ally at 50%.

Code from the class script

These are the calculation blocks from combat/pressure_formula.lua. The full function calculates ratio, the three damage rates and attacker counts before these lines. hot2 and hot4 are estimated healing amounts divided by maximum HP.

local focus_mult = 1.0 +
    0.06 * clamp(recent_attackers - 1, 0, 3) +
    0.20 * persistent_attackers
fast_pressure = focus_mult *
    (0.45 * d075 + 0.35 * d075_2 + 0.20 * d2_4)
slow_pressure = focus_mult *
    (0.15 * d075 + 0.45 * d075_2 + 0.40 * d2_4)

local hot2 = math.max(0, safe(input.hot_healing_2s, 0)) / maximum
local hot4 = math.max(0, safe(input.hot_healing_4s, 0)) / maximum
local projected2 = clamp(ratio - 2.0 * fast_pressure + 0.80 * hot2, 0, 1)
local projected4 = clamp(ratio - 4.0 * slow_pressure + 0.70 * hot4, 0, 1)
local net_pressure = math.max(0.001, slow_pressure - 0.70 * (hot4 / 4.0))
local ttd = ratio / net_pressure
path: Sage Seer Lua Healing Routine - Predictive Triage

items.title: How Seer uses it
items.text:
With Incoming Damage Formula selected, Seer can raise an ally's priority when predicted health or time to death shows urgent danger. It keeps current HP for ordinary cases. The tracker estimates healing over time from recent ticks of the player's tracked HoTs; it does not assume another healer will cast a rescue.

These are estimates from recent combat, not exact death times. If combat records are dropped, the tracker clears its history and stops using predictions while it gathers fresh data.

items.title: One action, one command owner
items.text: Hold the action key to attempt a configured ability on the current hostile target. Choose a learned ability before holding the key; the default is Force Stun. This script uses combat.ability_executor and keeps polling it after key release so the pending command can settle. It is a single-action script rather than a class rotation.

items.title: Before enabling
items.text:
Install the required shared helper: combat/ability_executor.lua must be available under your actual COMMON_PATH. This complete entry script does not include that module. A missing module fails at require during loading; inspect the selected script's Log tab.

Download single-action.lua and use the same file, Reload and Enable steps as the status panel. Under Controls, set Ability name to an ability your character knows and choose Action key before holding it against a hostile target.

items.title: Complete code
items.text:
local AbilityExecutor = require("combat.ability_executor")
local executor = AbilityExecutor.new()
local ID = "example_single_action"
gos.settings.register(ID, {
  title = "Example: Single Action", version = 1,
  activation = { mode = "hold", label = "Action key", default = "mouse4" },
  fields = {{ key = "ability", type = "string", label = "Ability name", default = "Force Stun", max_length = 96 }},
})
gos.on_tick(function()
  executor:tick() -- Poll even after the activation key is released.
  local settings = gos.settings.get(ID)
  if not settings.enabled or not settings.active then
    if executor:has_pending() then executor:cancel("inactive") end
    return
  end
  if executor:has_pending() then return end
  local loadout = gos.abilities.loadout()
  if loadout.status ~= "ready" or not loadout.known[settings.ability] then return end
  local world = gos.world()
  local target = world.current_target
  if not world.player or not target or target:reaction() ~= "hostile" then return end
  local hp = target:hp()
  if not hp or hp.current <= 0 then return end
  if not gos.abilities.can_cast(settings.ability, target).ok then return end
  executor:submit(settings.ability, target, {
    idempotencyKey = "example_action:" .. target:handle(),
    target_fallback = "none",
  })
end)
