items.title: Separate readiness, submission and activation
items.text:
Can it be attempted now? gos.abilities.can_cast reports a current local readiness result. Pending or unavailable checks do not own a command. wait_ms is observed timing, not a future scheduling promise.

Was it queued? gos.abilities.cast can accept a request for asynchronous processing. Keep the returned command handle; do not repeat the submission on every tick while it is owned.

Did it start? Inspect command status. acknowledged and activation_proven are start evidence. terminal only marks a lifecycle boundary: terminal submitted does not prove activation, and retained status may gain an outcome later.

items.title: Readiness is not queue eligibility
items.text: can_cast() tests current readiness. Omitted-target cast() requests can have different queue admission while a GCD or channel is ending. Explicit units/handles use ready-now admission, even when currently selected. See target and readiness semantics before choosing a pre-cast gate.

items.title: Keep one owner
items.text:
For continuous behavior, use one ability executor at the top level and pass it to sub-routes. Poll it from the top-level callback. A sub-route must check that the retained idempotency_key identifies its own route before canceling it. Continue polling after an activation key is released, including when cancellation fails.

The single-action example shows this structure.

items.title: Choose the target
items.text:
Pass a current unit or its opaque handle for an explicit target. An explicit cast does not persistently change the visible selected target by default. Use gos.target.select only for an intentional persistent selection change; confirm the later snapshot.

An explicit target defaults to target_fallback="none"; selecting "selected" permits a failed explicit target to use the selected unit instead. When omitting the target, omit target_fallback too: even "none" is invalid then.

items.title: Track selection separately
items.text:
gos.target.select(unit, target_intent?) can return an opaque third-value request handle. Poll gos.target.status instead of repeating submissions. observed confirms a matching selection snapshot; unconfirmed is not proof of no side effect. gos.target.cancel only cancels queued work, never undoes a dispatched selection. For overlay clicks, use the returned pressed entity, stable session generation and immutable intent ticket, not the current occupant of a reordered row. See the world and target contracts.

Core keeps a bounded command history. A known terminal expired status with command_history_expired permits releasing ownership; it carries no gameplay outcome. An unknown handle is a different result.

items.title: Do not infer outcomes from timers
items.text: A GCD change, cooldown movement, or empty current-cast field does not identify which command succeeded or failed. Use command status rather than a guessed timeout. Exact fields and result codes are in the ability reference.

items.title: Choose the stream, not a snapshot
items.text: gos.events.combat(cursor) is the ordered event stream. The initial call with no cursor subscribes at the current head; it does not replay a whole earlier fight. Keep the returned cursor for subsequent calls. The casts and instants helpers describe current presentation snapshots and are not a historical log.

items.title: Source and destination are different
items.text: For outgoing damage compare event.source_handle to the player's handle. For incoming damage compare event.target_handle. The optional combat_events module's player and target scopes match destinations. A unit may no longer resolve by the time you process an event; its captured identity is still useful for comparison, but its current health or position is unknown.

items.title: Retain actor labels with their epoch
items.text: Use optional source_name and target_name for captured display text. Keep each retained actor's actor_epoch with its handle; names are not grouping keys. For a later label, read gos.actor_names(handles, saved_epoch) in bounded update batches, including after the last combat hit. Preserve a delivered name when metadata is no longer retained. If the epoch changes, keep the old history's captured labels and stop enriching it from the new session. Resolving an event handle for current health or position also requires a matching actor epoch. See the actor metadata contract.

items.title: Bound processing and disclose gaps
items.text: Each stream call returns up to 64 events with more and dropped. Use a fixed pass budget and carry the cursor forward. Do not loop until the stream is empty without a cap. A dropped count means overwritten input, not zero damage. Show that a graph or total is incomplete.

items.title: Classify only supported evidence
items.text:
Classify by the published kind, optional action, and result, rather than ability-name substrings. An interrupted or immune action counts as damage only when the event says damage and supplies an amount. Keep unrecognized values unknown, or explicitly exclude them from the tool's totals.

When a tool retains data, bound both record count and age. Cache metadata outside hot processing and show the distinction between current observations and last-known presentation. See the counter example and public event schema.

items.title: Your first Lua script
items.text:
Choose how you want to start:

  1. Use existing scripts. With Core running, press Insert, open Official Script Library, then press Refresh. Choose a published script and version and click Install. Core installs the package and its declared shared dependencies at the required versions. Enable the installed script in Scripts; shared libraries have no separate entry to enable. This is the normal installation route for official packages.
  2. Develop your own script. The rest of this tutorial teaches creating and running your own local Lua entry script, starting with the read-only status panel. Continue below for the local-file, reload and enable steps.
path: Install SWTOR Scripts or Write Your First Lua Script

items.title: Install and run your first script
items.text:
With GoS:SWTOR Core already running in the game:

  1. Press Insert to open the Core menu. The Scripts list on the left is the Lua manager used in this guide.
  2. Click Open Folder to open the actual configured active-script directory. Hovering that button also shows its path. Folders shows the Script folder setting; it selects the parent containing live and common. When that setting is blank, the popup shows Current: for the active script folder's parent. Use the folder opened by Open Folder for entry scripts; a development checkout is not required.
  3. Download status-panel.lua into that opened folder, or copy the complete code into a plain-text file named status-panel.lua there. Check that the saved filename ends in .lua, not .lua.txt. Put it directly in the active folder.
  4. Click Reload to discover the new file. It appears disabled in Scripts. Select status-panel.lua and click Enable, or tick its checkbox in the list. The selected script's title becomes Example: Status Panel after loading.
  5. Open its Overlay tab and turn on Show panel (on by default). A small health label should appear. If the player or health snapshot is unavailable, it says Health: unavailable. This example never casts or changes targets.
  6. Open the selected script's Log tab with INFO enabled. The example logs SCRIPT_PATH (its active-script directory) and COMMON_PATH (its actual shared-module root) once when loaded. Use those values when placing files. Do not infer the shared root from a portable script's location.

After editing a saved file, click Reload again. Reload recreates callbacks and module state for enabled scripts. If you deliberately change Script folder in Folders, Apply & Reload applies that setting and reloads; it does not move your files.
path: Install SWTOR Scripts or Write Your First Lua Script

items.title: Find the script log and fix errors
items.text:
Select the script, then open Log. Load/reload failures appear as Reload failed: above the log; hovering the script's status dot also shows its status message. Callback errors are ERROR entries. An unhandled error disables that callback until scripts reload: fix the file and click Reload.

print and gos.log.info appear under INFO, which also includes SUCCESS. Turn on DEBUG to see gos.log.debug; it is hidden by default. Keep ERROR enabled and clear Search logs when looking for a missing message. The status panel logs its roots at load time, so it need not draw anything to confirm loading.

Save writes the selected script's retained log and reports the saved path. By default, status-panel.log.txt is saved beside status-panel.lua; Folders > Lua log folder can configure another location. See Logging for the message API. Saved files also include request diagnostics; review the contents and personal paths before sharing an excerpt.
path: Install SWTOR Scripts or Write Your First Lua Script

items.title: Follow the update callback
items.text:
Settings are registered once when the script loads. A callback is registered with gos.on_tick. Each callback reads a fresh world, performs bounded work, and returns. A requested interval is a scheduling cadence, not an exact timer guarantee.

Use gos.settings.get inside the callback to read current enablement and values. Registration is load-time-only. The embedded runtime is Lua 5.4.8, with the sandboxed libraries described in Runtime and data. The manager's General > Lua Version value is the script's registered settings version, not the embedded Lua language version.
path: Install SWTOR Scripts or Write Your First Lua Script

items.title: Add one feature at a time
items.text: Try the incoming damage counter to read combat events. Then use the single-action example to learn how to submit an ability and follow its command status. Single Action also needs the shared ability-executor module; the status panel needs no helper package.
path: Install SWTOR Scripts or Write Your First Lua Script

items.title: Common mistakes
items.text:
A GosUnit belongs to one world generation. Store its handle when identity must survive a tick, then resolve it in a fresh world. An old unit object cannot be reused after its generation changes.

nil is unavailable, not zero. pending is not absent. A successful queue submission is not proof that an ability started. File and network operations do not belong in a tick callback.

items.title: Where to look next
items.text: Runtime and data explains snapshot lifetimes and units. Continue with module authoring, or use the API reference to look up a particular call. Forum and contributions links to support, the official scripts repository and the contribution workflow.

items.title: Reusable helper modules
items.text: These optional modules load from the shared common root in packages that include them. They build on the public Lua API.

items.title: Make the helper modules available
items.text:
These are Lua files supplied by packages, not built-in gos functions. The GoS Common package includes combat/ability_executor.lua. Core installs the exact shared dependency requested by an official routine through Official Script Library. Shared packages have no entry script to enable separately.

For a local example such as Single Action, first check that combat/ability_executor.lua exists under the actual COMMON_PATH reported by the status panel. If it is missing, obtain that module from the official package and copy it into COMMON_PATH while keeping the combat subdirectory, then click Reload. That executor module has no other require dependencies. Other helpers may need more files; keep the dependencies listed by their package together. Do not overwrite shared modules used by installed routines with an unrelated version. A missing module is a load error to fix in Log, not a reason to remove the require or replace the executor.

items.title: ability_executor
items.text:
Use one executor for a top-level rotation and pass it to sub-routes. The top-level callback polls it; a route cancels only a command it owns.

This fragment assumes your script supplies Settings, should_cast and target_or_nil. Single Action supplies a complete entry script once the helper above is available.

local AbilityExecutor = require("combat.ability_executor")
local executor = AbilityExecutor.new()

gos.on_tick(function()
  executor:tick()

  if not Settings.active then
    if executor:owns_command() then
      executor:cancel("inactive")
    end
    return
  end

  if executor:can_submit() and should_cast then
    executor:submit("Ability Name", target_or_nil, {
      idempotencyKey = "route-action",
    })
  end
end)

items.title: Ownership and submission
items.text:
Method Use new() Create the top-level executor. tick() Poll its command and refresh at most one retained receipt. Call even after the activation key is released. owns_command() / can_submit() Check whether it owns a command / can submit another. submit(ability, target, options) Attempt an action with a required nonempty idempotencyKey. can_replace() / replace(...) Check and request replacement of its current command. cancel(reason) Request cancellation; keep polling until ownership ends. status() Read a copy of the last observation published by tick() or an operation.

idempotencyKey belongs to the helper, not native cast options. Repeating the same key, ability and target while owned deduplicates the request. A busy result is not automatically adopted: adoptBusy=true also requires a retained receipt matching the handle, key, ability and target.

The explicit-target fallback defaults to none. Omit target_fallback when the target is nil; even "none" is invalid without an explicit target. expectedStartAt and timeout are rejected with unsupported_executor_lifecycle_option. Missing idempotencyKey returns idempotency_key_required; invalid options submit no native command.

items.title: Results and receipts
items.text:
An operation result describes both the attempted action and any command still owned by the executor:

  • accepted (ok for compatibility) can be true for a deduplicated request; new_command says whether it created a command.
  • owns_command, blocks_submission, can_submit and can_replace describe current ownership. admission_pending alone acquires no command.
  • request_ability / request_idempotency_key identify the attempted action; ability / idempotency_key identify the retained command.
  • disposition is the helper's interpretation; nested core contains native status. See command outcomes.

A receipt is a copied observation retained by the helper, not a command itself. receipt(handle) returns that copy or nil; receipts(limit) returns newest first, with at most 16 retained independently of Core's history. terminal_state(core_status) projects a native status into a helper disposition. It maps an expired Core-history tombstone to failed; check core.state and core.reason before treating that as a failed ability.

Compatibility aliases: has_pending() is owns_command(); last_receipts(limit) is receipts(limit).

items.title: combat_events
items.text:
Register destination-scoped handlers at load time. The module owns one combat cursor and polling callback for the importing script; your script does not poll it.

local Combat = require("combat.combat_events")

Combat.on_player("damage", function(event)
  gos.log.info("Player damage", event.amount)
end)
Registration Event destination Combat.on_player(name, callback) Local player Combat.on_current_target(name, callback) Current selected target Combat.on_ally(name, callback) Currently resolved friendly unit other than the player

The name matches event.kind or event.action. Delivery preserves stream order; the module logs dropped records. The log call above illustrates delivery; for a meter, accumulate a bounded model instead of logging each hit.

Scopes use the world at poll time, not event-time selection or teams. The helper does not check actor epochs. For outgoing events or history that can cross a world-session change, read gos.events.combat directly, compare source_handle when appropriate and apply the epoch check before resolving historical handles.

items.title: Write reusable modules
items.text: Put formatting, event histories and decision logic in modules that a top-level script can load with require.
path: SWTOR Lua Scripting - Write Reusable Addon Modules

items.title: Separate responsibilities
items.text:
A top-level script owns settings, activation and callbacks. Plain modules can transform copied data without registering callbacks. An event collector can maintain a bounded model. A presentation callback draws that prepared model. When commands are involved, exactly one top-level executor owns them and is passed to routes.

A small project can consist of an entry point in the active scripts root and shared files such as my_tool_model.lua and my_tool_format.lua in the approved common root. Load them with require("my_tool_model"). Module state is cached per top-level script environment, not shared global state across every script.

Use Getting started to locate the actual SCRIPT_PATH and COMMON_PATH for your installation. Packaged helpers have their own availability requirements.

A Lua reload recreates callbacks and module state. Successful Official Script Library installs, updates and removals reload enabled scripts automatically, including local scripts. Make load-time initialization safe to repeat.
path: SWTOR Lua Scripting - Write Reusable Addon Modules

items.title: Example: a plain Lua module
items.text:
-- my_tool_format.lua
local Format = {}
function Format.health(hp)
  if not hp or hp.percent == nil then return "unknown" end
  return string.format("%.0f%%", hp.percent)
end
return Format

Use it from another script:

local Format = require("my_tool_format")
gos.on_tick(function()
  local player = gos.world().player
  local text = Format.health(player and player:hp() or nil)
  -- Draw the prepared text or store it in your presentation model.
end, { interval_ms = 100 })

For histories, see the bounded ring-buffer module. Retain copied scalar data or opaque handles, not generation-bound world or unit objects.

See Runtime and data for available Lua libraries and sandbox file helpers for permitted load-time resources.
path: SWTOR Lua Scripting - Write Reusable Addon Modules

items.title: Keep each update finite
items.text:
Read one current world per callback. Prefer the player or selected target when that is all you need. Filter a unit query once and process a fixed maximum number of rows appropriate to the tool. Avoid nested all-unit scans and sorting the same unchanged data on every tick.

Use interval_ms for display work that does not need every update. The status panel uses 100 ms; input edges and command polling may need every update.

items.title: Consume new events, not old history
items.text:
Retain the combat cursor, process only returned records, and cap the number of batches per callback. Each call yields at most 64 events. If more remains true, leave the rest for a later update. Track dropped; incomplete input must not look like a complete fight.

The incoming damage example uses at most four batches and keeps totals rather than storing every hit. A graph needs a fixed-capacity buffer or fixed time buckets. Never grow one table for an entire session without an eviction policy.

items.title: Prepare, then draw
items.text:
Maintain a small model and render from it. Use stable short drawing IDs so an update replaces an existing element. Use retained frame=true drawings for current callback output, and TTL drawings for intentionally persistent markers. Do not use long TTLs to disguise stale gameplay data.

One registered callback can retain at most 192 frame commands. Core combines at most 512 active drawing commands overall, with at most 32 callbacks retaining frame output. A drawing is replaced only when its callback owner, target, draw kind and ID match. These budgets are shared with other scripts.

items.title: Avoid expensive work in ticks
items.text:
Do not download, unzip, read or write files, rebuild lookup maps, emit per-event logs, or run blocking loops inside frequent callbacks. Prepare static data at load time. Log meaningful transitions with a bounded rate; store totals in memory instead of writing every observation.

Measure the tool with representative entity and event counts.

items.title: Runtime and data
items.text: Scripts run in isolated Lua environments on Core's update cadence. Register work with gos.on_tick; do not create a render loop or blocking loop.

items.title: Snapshot lifetime and identity
items.text:
GosWorld and GosUnit values belong to one update generation. Retain a unit's opaque handle when identity must survive a tick, then resolve it in a fresh world. Across a world-session change, also check the saved actor epoch.

Ability, unit, effect and command handles are opaque strings: compare them or pass them back to Core. Do not parse them or persist them across game sessions.

nil means an optional observation is unavailable. Check a result table's status before reading its payload. Missing or pending data does not mean zero, false, or absence.

items.title: Units
items.text:
Values Unit Ability cooldowns, cast times, effect timers, overlay TTL Seconds gos.time_ms(), event timestamp, result wait_ms, effect age_ms Milliseconds Position, distance and velocity coordinates Game-world coordinate scale; one world unit is ten metres Health and resource percentages 0..100

unit:distance() needs matched spatial samples for both the player and unit; unit:position() needs one for that unit. Either returns nil when the required sample is unavailable. Convert range thresholds once: 30 metres is 3 world units.

items.title: Lua environment
items.text:
Core embeds Lua 5.4.8. This is the language/runtime version, independent of a script's gos.settings.register(..., { version = ... }) settings version.

The global gos table and its child tables are read-only. Selected Lua base functions and the table, string, math, UTF-8, and coroutine libraries are available, with os.clock, os.date, os.difftime, os.time, and debug.traceback. Coroutines are cooperative, not background threads.

Use the sandboxed require for modules and the file helpers for permitted files. Process execution, unrestricted operating-system access, bytecode loading and native modules are unavailable. load, loadfile, dofile, rawget, rawset, and collectgarbage are not exposed.

items.title: Support and script contributions
items.text:
Use the GoS:SWTOR feature and support thread on the Gaming On Steroids forum. For a particular official script, use its discussion link in Official Script Library (the globe button); hover it to check the destination. The Operative / Scoundrel thread is one example.

The public official-scripts repository contains the distributed Lua packages, READMEs and changelogs. Read its package format before proposing a package change. Fork that repository and open a pull request with the proposed patch, required helpers and a clear statement of what you tested. Include the matching README/changelog changes for user-facing behavior. Published version folders are immutable: describe a fix against an existing version as a proposed change, not a replacement release with the same version. Maintainers review/test accepted changes, carry them into the development source with attribution, and export a new package version and catalog update.

For documentation corrections or a new example, open a documentation pull request with the page URL and proposed text/code. The public repository includes editable Markdown pages; its contribution guide explains which files to edit. You can also post a correction in the support thread. State whether an example is a complete script or a fragment, which helper files it requires, and whether it was tested in game. Maintainers review accepted corrections before rebuilding and publishing the site.
path: Share scripts and ask useful questions

items.title: Link directly to the relevant contract
items.text:
Open the API entry or guide, select the heading link, and copy its URL into your forum post. Each callable has a stable page. Search can find names such as gos.abilities.cast, definition_key, or incoming damage.

A useful question includes the observed behavior, the expected behavior, the relevant public API entry, and a short reproducible Lua snippet. Include any pending, unavailable or truncated result fields.
path: Share scripts and ask useful questions

items.title: Keep reports minimal and private
items.text: Share only the snippet and public result fields needed to explain the problem. Remove account identifiers, character names, credentials, personal paths and unrelated logs before posting.
path: Share scripts and ask useful questions

items.title: Contribute more than reference entries
items.text: Examples, explanations of data availability, bounded data structures, UI patterns and module organization are all useful documentation contributions. Label fragments versus complete scripts, list required helper modules, and distinguish static review from in-game testing.
